title: Committee of Supply debate on Manpower Ministry budget and labour policies
what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head S (Manpower) of the Estimates, opened by Ms Yeo Wan Ling moving a $100 reduction amendment, with MPs raising labour policy proposals and ministers responding.
why_it_matters: The transcript records planned changes including adding eight occupations to the NTS-OL in 2026, raising EP and S Pass qualifying salaries and the Local Qualifying Salary, extending GRIT to the 2026 cohort, and expanding the Overseas Markets Immersion Programme. It also records proposals from MPs on retrenchment benefits, jobseeker support, caregiver leave, and wage thresholds, but does not state that these proposals will be adopted.

key_points.point: Ms Yeo Wan Ling moved an amendment to reduce the total sum allocated for Head S of the Estimates by $100.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
key_points.quote: That the total sum to be allocated for Head S of the Estimates be reduced by $100.

key_points.point: She said Singapore is going through a period of profound labour change.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
key_points.quote: Singapore is going through a period of profound labour change.

key_points.point: She said platform work remains inherently precarious.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
key_points.quote: platform work remains inherently precarious.

key_points.point: She said stronger safeguards are needed beyond baseline protections.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
key_points.quote: We need to move beyond baseline protections.

key_points.point: She put forward attracting top global talent as a Budget priority.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
key_points.quote: First, we must continue attracting top global talent in a way that strengthens, not substitutes our Singaporean core.

key_points.point: She noted the Ministry's intention to add eight occupations from social services, food services and transportation to the NTS-OL in 2026.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
key_points.quote: I note the Ministry's intention to add eight occupations from the social services, food services and transportation sectors to the Non-traditional Sources Occupation List (NTS-OL) in 2026.

key_points.point: Mr Pritam Singh said the time has come to legislate retrenchment benefits as a norm.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: The time has come for these guidelines to be legislated as a norm in an advanced economy like Singapore

key_points.point: He proposed that larger companies with more than 25 workers pay at least one month per year of service.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: Larger companies, those with more than 25 workers, should be expected to pay more at minimum, one month for every year of service, which is the norm for unionised companies.

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan proposed that retrenchment notice be given prior to retrenchment.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: I propose that the notice be done prior to retrenchment, so that early support can be activated

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Terence Ho suggested extending free or subsidised access to AI premium tools to a larger group of Singaporeans.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho
key_points.quote: I would like to suggest that the Ministry consider extending free or subsidised access to AI premium tools to a larger group of Singaporeans

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim proposed a national OJT system for apprenticeships, internships and mentorships.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: I propose that we institutionalise a national OJT system for apprenticeships, internships and mentorships.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye asked whether there have been measurable sectoral productivity gains in PWM sectors.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: I therefore ask MOM, have we seen measurable sectoral productivity gains in PWM sectors?

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim proposed raising the Workfare Income Supplement income threshold to $3,500.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: I believe that it is time to disproportionately raise the income threshold for the Workfare Income Supplement to $3,500

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song proposed a Youth Wage Credit Scheme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
key_points.quote: I propose a Youth Wage Credit Scheme.

key_points.point: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan suggested the new agency develop practical tool kits for portfolio-based assessment and skills-first hiring.
key_points.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan
key_points.quote: First, for the new agency to develop practical tool kits that employers can use for portfolio-based assessment and skills-first hiring.

key_points.point: Mr Mark Lee noted that the Employment Pass qualifying salary will rise from $4,500 to $6,000 next year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
key_points.quote: Since 2020, the Employment Pass (EP) qualifying salary will rise from $4,500 to $6,000 next year

key_points.point: Mr Shawn Loh proposed retaining the minimum wage increase to qualify for PWCS support at $100 instead of $200.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
key_points.quote: the minimum wage increase to qualify for PWCS support should be retained at $100 instead of the Government's change to set it at $200.

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal asked how MOM will measure whether enterprises are redesigning jobs alongside technology adoption.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: how will MOM measure whether enterprises are redesigning jobs alongside technology adoption?

key_points.point: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo proposed introducing a national career health screening.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
key_points.quote: introduce a national career health screening.

key_points.point: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen called for promoting the message that skilled trades are essential work and a respected choice.
key_points.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen
key_points.quote: skilled trades are essential work and a respected choice

key_points.point: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether the Government would consider developing a National Master Trades Accreditation framework.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: Would the Government consider developing a National Master Trades Accreditation framework

key_points.point: Mr Ng Chee Meng asked whether Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications can be brought forward to enable earlier support.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Ministry whether the Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications can be brought forward to enable earlier and better support to retrenched workers

key_points.point: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari asked how the Ministry tracks outcomes and ensures senior employment rates are not affected, especially for those aged 55 to 64.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari
key_points.quote: how does the Ministry track outcomes and ensure senior employment rates are not affected, especially for those aged 55 to 64?

key_points.point: Dr Tan See Leng said GRIT will be extended to include the 2026 cohort.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: We will extend it to include the 2026 cohort as well.

key_points.point: Dr Tan See Leng said the Overseas Markets Immersion Programme is being expanded to more companies and potentially younger employees.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we are now doing is to expand it to more companies, to even potentially to younger employees as well who join companies.

key_points.point: Dr Tan See Leng said the national master trade work will start with three sectors, including plumbers and air-conditioning technicians.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: The other two trades that we have identified is plumber and then the third one is air-conditioning technicians.

key_points.point: Dr Tan See Leng said there are no plans to develop GRIT into a national programme.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we do not have plans to develop this into a national programme.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon said MOM will consider Company Training Committee-style support for mid-career PMEs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: The answer is yes, because the Company Training Committee structure and the format is really a means to an end.

key_points.point: Dr Tan See Leng said the review of the Employment Act will look at mandatory retrenchment notification comprehensively.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we are undertaking the review of the Employment Act and we will look at all that comprehensively.

key_points.point: Dr Tan See Leng said the Government consults widely with workers, employers, unions and industry partners.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: We consult widely with workers, with employers, with unions, with industry partners

key_points.point: Ms Yeo Wan Ling sought leave to withdraw her amendment.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
key_points.quote: I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.

what_happens_next: The Chairman invited Ms Yeo Wan Ling to withdraw her amendment, and she sought leave to withdraw it.
